title: Charge
subtitle: Move sideways. Let the boss miss. Counterattack.
summary: The boss aims, locks its direction, and charges forward. It cannot turn after the lock.
learning: Wait for the lock, move out of the lane, then counterattack.

demo.title: See how Charge works
demo.intro: Compare moving sideways with running straight away.
phaseDescriptions: The boss can still turn toward the player.
The direction is fixed. Move sideways out of the lane.
The boss moves along the fixed line.
demo.reducedMotion: Animation starts paused. Use the phase buttons or timeline to explore without playback.
demo.diagramDescription: The boss charges toward the player. Moving sideways avoids the attack; running straight away leads to a hit.
demo.overlayNote: The colored lane explains the mechanic. A real game may telegraph it through pose, sound, or effects.

steps.title: Wait for the commitment
steps.body: Wait for the cue that says the direction is fixed. Before that, the boss can still turn.

steps.title: Move across the line
steps.body: Move sideways until the whole player is outside the danger lane.

steps.title: Punish the miss
steps.body: Attack after the boss stops, before its next action begins.

mistakes.title: Running along the lane
mistakes.body: You stay inside the danger lane, so the boss can still hit you.

mistakes.title: Dodging too early
mistakes.body: Before the lock, the boss can turn and follow you.

designNotes.title: Make commitment visible
designNotes.body: Show a clear cue when the boss stops tracking the player.

designNotes.title: Leave a reachable escape
designNotes.body: Give enough time to escape with normal movement.

designNotes.title: Give recovery a purpose
designNotes.body: Keep the boss still long enough for the player to counterattack.

story.title: Use a clear arena
story.body: A long, open lane makes the attack easy to read. Avoid obstacles that hide the boss or the escape route.

adaptation.title: Respect player upgrades
adaptation.body: Test the attack against the abilities already available to the player. If the boss blocks an attack, show it clearly and keep another response useful.

distinction.title: Charge ≠ dash ≠ lunge
distinction.body: A charge threatens a full lane. A dash changes position. A lunge is a short attack. This page shows one kind of charge.

quiz.question: The direction is fixed. What is the reliable escape in this example?
options: Run straight away from the boss.
Move sideways until your whole body leaves the lane.
Stand still and wait for recovery.
quiz.explanation: Move sideways. After the lock, the boss cannot follow. Running along the same line keeps the player in danger.
